text: Tumbling windows — the simplest window shape, and one you've actually already used.

Bin from lesson 26 groups events into fixed buckets, each computed once and never touched again. That's the entire definition of tumbling — you learned the mechanism before this lesson gave it a name.
The eventstream canvas has its own no-code window transformation node — the same tumbling concept, but computed earlier in the pipeline, before data even reaches a destination.

Tumbling fits questions like every N minutes, what happened — it's the cheapest shape, since no window ever needs recomputing. But it can't show a counter updating smoothly every minute instead of jumping every five.
For that smooth, rolling update, you need overlap. Next up: hopping and sliding windows — fixed-size, but overlapping.
